[Explore this instance](https://hodge.computer/#case/four-plus-two-residual) · [Exact statement](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/blob/main/data/four-plus-two-residual/instance.rec) · [Mathematical context](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/blob/main/data/four-plus-two-residual/why.md)

Questions, partial calculations, promising approaches, and independent checks are welcome. Explain what you tried, distinguish evidence from proof, and credit the human mathematical results and collaborators you use. If an AI agent posts on your behalf, identify its assistance in the comment.

This thread is shared with the website. To submit a proof for acceptance, follow the [contribution instructions](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and open a solution PR. A discussion comment does not replace a checked proof.

nodes.body:
### The binary contribution is a three-dimensional Prym, and the visible elliptic quotient misses the source

The $4+2$ splitting gives an explicit character calculation identifying the binary factor used by the target. Divisor support is supplied by the [two-reflection theorem](https://hodge.computer/#technical-information/weighted-threefolds); the [fixed-core contact calculation](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/discussions/120#discussioncomment-19448881) constructs a serving family on this exact equation. The calculation below explains why the visible elliptic quotient alone cannot replace that correspondence.

Write the [fixed equation](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/blob/faa9df2ec6406e4eacc135f677cf3711315d0e41/data/four-plus-two-residual/instance.rec) as $F=H(X_0,X_1,Y_0,Y_1)+B(x,y)$, where $(x,y)=(X_2,Y_2)$ and

$$
B(x,y)=x^6+\frac{15}{7}x^4y^2+\frac{10}{7}x^2y^4+y^6.
$$

The natural binary triple cover is $C_B:z^3=B(x,y)\subset\mathbf P(1,1,2)$. On $x=1$, with $t=y/x$ and $w=z/x^2$, it is

$$
w^3=b(t),\qquad b(t)=1+\frac{15}{7}t^2+\frac{10}{7}t^4+t^6.
$$

The polynomial is separable: modulo $5$ it is $1+t^6$, coprime to its derivative. The curve has genus four. A basis of its holomorphic differentials is

$$
\frac{dt}{w},\qquad \frac{dt}{w^2},\qquad \frac{t\thinspace dt}{w^2},\qquad \frac{t^2dt}{w^2}.
$$

At infinity $w$ has pole order two, so $t^i dt/w^j$ is regular precisely when $i\le2j-2$ for $j=1,2$; at the six finite branch points all four displayed forms are regular. This also gives the basis directly.

Let $\sigma(t,w)=(-t,w)$ and $\delta(t,w)=(t,\zeta_3w)$. The $\sigma$-invariant holomorphic line is $t\thinspace dt/w^2$. The anti-invariant space is

$$
H^{1,0}(C_B)^-=\left\langle\frac{dt}{w},\frac{dt}{w^2},\frac{t^2dt}{w^2}\right\rangle,
$$

with deck multiplicities $1$ for $\zeta_3^2$ and $2$ for $\zeta_3$. Therefore the anti-invariant abelian factor, equivalently the connected Prym of $C_B\to C_B/\sigma$, has dimension three and $\mathbf Q(\zeta_3)$ signature $(2,1)$, up to the ordering of embeddings.

The invariant quotient itself is the elliptic curve

$$
w^3=1+\frac{15}{7}v+\frac{10}{7}v^2+v^3,\qquad v=t^2.
$$

Its deck automorphism has order three and fixed points, so its $j$-invariant is $0$. But it is the wrong involution sector for the target. The prescribed numerator $A=X_0^3Y_0^3$ is unchanged by $Y_2\mapsto-Y_2$, while the projective volume changes sign. Hence the residue is anti-invariant under this reflection. Projection to the displayed elliptic quotient kills the binary component of this residue.

One can also track the exact deck character in the usual split-cover residue decomposition. In the ordinary sixth covers $U^6=H$ and $V^6=B$, the core $H^{2,1}$ residue has numerator $AU$, and the binary $H^{1,0}$ residue has numerator $V^3$. Their deck characters, including volume, are respectively $\zeta_6^2$ and $\zeta_6^4$. They descend under $u=U^2$ and $w=V^2$ to opposite order-three characters on

$$
T_H:u^3=H\subset\mathbf P(1,1,1,1,2),\qquad C_B.
$$

The binary holomorphic factor is the $\zeta_3^2$ line $dt/w$, which is indeed anti-invariant. The core factor is also anti-invariant under $(Y_0,Y_1)\mapsto(-Y_0,-Y_1)$: its volume is even and $A$ is odd. These two signs agree with the invariance of the original residue under the global $Y$ sign.

This explains concretely which support contribution is absent from the elementary ternary-split companion argument alone. The weighted companions are

$$
W_H:\space H+s^3+t^3=0\subset\mathbf P(1,1,1,1,2,2),\qquad
W_B:\space B+s^3+t^3=0\subset\mathbf P(1,1,2,2).
$$

Weighted adjunction gives a Fano fourfold for $W_H$, while the quasismooth model of $W_B$ resolves to a K3 surface. The $3+3$ construction has two Fano-supported factors and contracts a common elliptic factor; here the K3 side has no automatic corresponding support gain. Merely replacing its binary input by the visible elliptic quotient would remove the desired character.

The weighted-threefold correspondence supplies this support without identifying the Prym with a product of CM elliptic curves. The signature calculation alone supplies neither such a splitting nor a definite-unitary finite-monodromy argument in a varying family. It also does not prove that this individual Prym is simple or exclude an exceptional splitting. These character calculations explain the limitation of the visible elliptic quotient; extracting a literal rational primitive from the serving correspondence is the separate calculation described in the fixed-core comment.

This uses the project's [split and K3 framework](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/blob/faa9df2ec6406e4eacc135f677cf3711315d0e41/docs/03a-split-and-k3.md), with explicit differential and character calculations above. ChatGPT-assisted investigation for `benediamond`, including separate AI-agent checks; no independent human review, Lean proof, or solve is claimed.

### Wave-2 referee pass: every certificate for this instance has $\deg D \ge 6$ (exact), plus exact degree-6 exclusions

Prepared for `kejace` with Claude (Anthropic) assistance; no human review yet; nothing Lean-verified; no certificate claimed.

**Setting.** $F = H(X_0,X_1,Y_0,Y_1) + B(X_2,Y_2)$, $q = 1$, $A = X_0^3Y_0^3$. A certificate with denominator $D$ (coprime to $F$) satisfies $A D^2 - D\,N(F) + F\,(D\operatorname{div}N - N(D)) = F^2 Q$; reducing modulo $F$ gives (E1) $N(F) = AD + mF$, i.e. $[A][D] = 0$ in $R(F) = S/J(F)$, and the rest is (E2). Everything below was computed by an agent session (packet linked at the end) and then independently replayed by a referee pass with separate code (exact over $\mathbb{Q}$ with python-flint, or modulo the fresh prime $10^9+9$); "exact" means field-independent linear algebra, so the statements hold over $\mathbb{C}$.

**1. E1 structure (exact).** Since the variables split, $R(F) = R(H)\otimes R(B)$ and $\ker([A]\colon R(F)_d \to R(F)_{d+6}) = \bigoplus_k \ker(a\cdot\colon R(H)_{d-k}\to R(H)_{d-k+6})\otimes R(B)_k$ with $a = X_0^3Y_0^3$. The core kernels modulo $J(H)_k$, by $(Y_0,Y_1)$-parity (even/odd), are $k\le 5$: $0/0$; $6$: $20/13$; $7$: $30/30$; $8$: $41/34$; $9$: $38/38$; $10$: $36/31$; $11$: $26/26$; $12$: $19/16$ (exact: $a\cdot$ is surjective for $k \ge 5$, so $\dim\ker = \dim R(H)_k - \dim R(H)_{k+6}$; the Hilbert functions of $R(H)$ and $R(B)$ are the complete-intersection ones over $\mathbb{Q}$). Hence **no E1-admissible denominator of degree $\le 4$ exists, in any parity**, and **every E1-admissible denominator of degree 5 is a polar $F_v = v\cdot\nabla F$, $v\in\mathbb{C}^6$.** This makes the earlier single-prime, $Y$-even screens (dossier, $p = 2^{31}-1$) exact and parity-free.

**2. Degree 5 is excluded over $\mathbb{C}$ (exact).** For $D = F_v$, E1 forces $N = Av + \tfrac{m}{6}z + K$ with $K$ Koszul (linear coefficients), and E2 reduces to $F_vA_v - A\,F_{vv} + F_v\operatorname{div}K - K(F_v) = FQ$ ($m$ cancels; $F_{vv} = v^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{Hess}(F)\,v$). Replacing $v\otimes v$ and $v\otimes\ell$ by free tensors gives a linear system (2078 equations, $21+540+126$ unknowns, rank 435 over $\mathbb{Q}$) whose kernel projects onto an 8-dimensional $W\subset\operatorname{Sym}^2\mathbb{C}^6$ spanned by the mixed core$\times$binary coordinates $e_ae_b$ ($a\in\{X_0,X_1,Y_0,Y_1\}$, $b\in\{X_2,Y_2\}$). Every $v_i^2$ vanishes on $W$, so $W$ contains no rank-one tensor, so no certificate has $\deg D = 5$. (Control: for a target in $J(F)$ the same code returns $W = \operatorname{Sym}^2$.) **Therefore $\deg D\ge 6$ for every certificate of this instance.** By the prescribed-support theorem of the book (ch. 1), at $q = 1$ this is a statement about supports: no certificate has poles confined to a hypersurface $V(D_{\mathrm{red}})$ with $\deg D_{\mathrm{red}}\le 5$.

**3. Degree 6 (partial).** E1-admissible sextics are $D = F_w + c$ with $w\in(S_1)^6$ (36 parameters) and $c$ in the 33-dimensional core-only kernel.
* *Jacobian type, $G$-eigenvectors (exact).* Under the diagonal symmetry group $G$ (order 24, generated by $(X_2,Y_2)\mapsto\zeta_6(X_2,Y_2)$, $X_2\mapsto -X_2$, $(Y_0,Y_1)\mapsto -(Y_0,Y_1)$) the eigenvector members of the Jacobian family fall into 11 character classes ($10 + 8 + 9\times 2$ parameters; the 10-parameter class contains all weighted Euler polars $\sum\lambda_a z_aF_a$). The sector-restricted Hessian relaxation of each class has no rank-one point, except the Euler line $D = 6\lambda F$ in the 10-parameter class (not coprime to $F$). **No $G$-eigenvector Jacobian-type sextic admits a certificate.** Non-eigenvector members ($w$ mixing characters) are not covered.
* *Fixed rational $D$, rigorous over $\mathbb{C}$ by the nullity argument* (inconsistent modulo $p$, and the exact rational nullity $n_m + \dim\{K\ \text{Koszul}: D\operatorname{div}K - K(D)\in F\cdot S\}$ equals the modular nullity): $B(X_2,Y_2)$ and $H(X_0,X_1,Y_0,Y_1)$ (both in $J(F)$; rank 2298 of 2602 unknowns, nullity 304); and every exact rational representative of the core-only E1 kernels of degrees 6, 7, 8 ($20+13$, $30+30$, $41+34$ representatives, plus 6 random same-parity combinations per degree), each tested in the character-sector-restricted full 6-variable system (lossless for these $G$-eigenvectors): all 186 inconsistent over $\mathbb{C}$. Mixed-parity kernel elements and the general $69$-parameter sextic family remain untested.

**4. Not done / open.** The sum-principle test of products $c(x)\,b(X_2,Y_2)$, generic E1-admissible members of degrees 7–10, and the core-kernel sweep for degrees 9–12 were planned but did not run (compute capacity); no result is claimed for them. Nothing here is a nonexistence statement: the open question remains whether some denominator of degree $\ge 6$ outside the tested families, or a correspondence supplying the missing Prym support identified by `benediamond` above, serves $A$.

**Reproduction.** Packet (scripts, JSON receipts, Singular inputs, referee replays in `referee/`, `README-referee.md`): https://github.com/kejace/sextics/tree/ae801eced7598ae8eca9943b6d206e3bcb53ac82/research/results/four-plus-two-residual/wave2-excl ; full exclusion report: https://github.com/kejace/sextics/blob/ae801eced7598ae8eca9943b6d206e3bcb53ac82/research/notes/wave2-four-plus-two-residual-excl.md ; referee report: https://github.com/kejace/sextics/blob/ae801eced7598ae8eca9943b6d206e3bcb53ac82/research/results/four-plus-two-residual/wave2-excl/referee/referee-report.md . Engine: python-flint 0.9.0, Singular 4.3.2, sympy 1.12. Credits: `benediamond` (character computation above, which fixes the target sector used here), the project book (certificate framework, prescribed-support theorem); the E1 kernel surjectivity argument is due to a parallel verification session.

### An explicit contact family spans the exact core's anti-invariant cohomology

An explicit family of curves on the **fixed** weighted core of this instance has a cylinder map surjecting onto all of its anti-invariant third cohomology. The general construction is in [Chapter 3B](https://hodge.computer/#technical-information/weighted-threefolds): norm contacts, Abel–Jacobi residues and the finite spanning criterion. [Chapter 2, §2.8](https://hodge.computer/#technical-information/explicit-constructions) gives the current and suspension formulas. This comment records the exact-instance calculation and the remaining extraction problem.

Mathematical certificate existence follows from the book's two-reflection theorem. The calculation here supplies a concrete serving correspondence on the prescribed equation, explicit closed differentials, and a finite algebra in which to attempt the rational identity. **It does not supply a `HasCertificate` proof or a displayed rational vector field.**

#### The fixed equation and actual moving family

Put $(a,b,c,d)=(X_0,X_1,Y_0,Y_1)$ and $\kappa=5/7$. The core is

$$
H=a^6+b^6+\kappa a^5b+2\kappa ab^5+c^6+d^6+\kappa c^5d+3\kappa cd^5+\kappa abcd(a^2+2c^2).
$$

We work on $T:(u^3+H=0)\subset\mathbf P(1,1,1,1,2)$ with $\sigma(a,b,c,d,u)=(a,b,-c,-d,u)$. The contact presentations satisfy

$$
u^3+H=f_1g_1+f_2g_2+A^2-B^2,
\qquad C_\tau=(f_1=f_2=A+B=0).
$$

The starting contact is a nodal union of two elliptic curves. A transverse slice of the presentation incidence has an ordinary node with two branches; both smooth all three curve nodes. Thus this is an actual algebraic family of smooth genus-four curves on this same $T$. The core equation stays fixed throughout. Reduction modulo five is used only to certify smoothness of $T$.

#### A full span, rather than a nonzero pairing

The normal obstruction functional $\ell(\tau)$ is computed from the degree-six quotient by $(f_1,f_2,g_1,g_2,A,B)$. Over $\mathbf F_{23}[v]/(v^2-15)$, the first 48 Taylor coefficient rows have a 48-by-48 minor

$$
22+2v,\qquad \mathrm{Norm}(22+2v)=10\ne0.
$$

The characteristic-zero lift is justified by the actual incidence equations and structural upper bounds on the central ranks; it is not an inference from modular rank alone. The branch equation is checked through order 66, and the obstruction annihilates all 72 ideal columns through order 64. Independent code reconstructs these checks. The projected ranks in the $u^0$ and $u^1$ sectors are respectively 32 and 16.

The book's normal-duality and spanning criterion therefore gives, for the proper normalization $\Gamma$ of the parameter curve,

$$
Z^{\ast}:H^{2,1}(T)^-\hookrightarrow H^{1,0}(\Gamma),
\qquad Z_{\ast}:H^1(\Gamma)(-1)\twoheadrightarrow H^3(T)^-.
$$

In particular $g(\Gamma)\ge48$. This parameter curve is distinct from its genus-four fibers in $T$. The result serves the whole anti-invariant core, including the target character identified in the Prym calculation; no splitting of the binary Prym is claimed.

#### Closed forms and a concrete trace problem

For $h=A+B$ and $\mathbf f=(f_1,f_2,h,g_1,g_2)$, the actual Abel–Jacobi pullbacks are

$$
\eta_R=\tau_{\mathbf f}(R\thinspace d_\Gamma h),
\qquad \tau_{\mathbf f}(\det\mathrm{Jac}\mathbf f)=96,
$$

up to the single orientation convention. These are holomorphic differentials on $\Gamma$, hence closed. At the recorded seed their normalization relative to the computed obstruction functional is the nonzero factor $17v$ modulo 23. This removes an unknown parameter-dependent scale from the construction.

On $(a,b,c,d)=(1,r,t,st)$, write $w^3=-P(t)$, where

$$
P(t)=1+r^6+\kappa r+2\kappa r^5+\kappa rs\thinspace t^2+2\kappa rs\thinspace t^4+(1+s^6+\kappa s+3\kappa s^5)t^6.
$$

The prescribed source becomes $t^4\thinspace dr\wedge ds\wedge dt/w^5$. The intrinsic contact chart has 26 parameters and 25 norm equations. Adding the two moving-point equations gives 27 equations in 27 unknowns over $\mathbf Q(r,s)$; dominance of the actual universal surface, not just this equation count, supplies a finite separable factor. The chart has been checked on the actual smoothing jets.

For the moving point $(\alpha,\beta)$, $\beta^3=-P(\alpha)$, the book's current is

$$
\eta\wedge\frac{\beta^2}{w^2}
\bigl(d\log(t-\alpha)-d\log(t+\alpha)\bigr).
$$

Its derivative has a literal source triple in the basis $(1,t^2,t^4)$. The packet gives the finite algebra and formulas, including cancellation of the apparent $\beta$ denominator. Twenty-two symbolic identities were checked, with an exact binary-contact trace as a control.

**The remaining calculation is significant.** Pulling back $R$ and pushing forward gives $K(R)=Z_{\ast}Z^{\ast}(R)$, not generally $R$. Polarization proves that $K$ is invertible; its compression to the relevant 32-dimensional character in $H^{2,1}$ is also invertible. Its entries have not been computed. Nor has the global trace on the 27-equation algebra. One must calculate an appropriate closed linear combination and its traced source, including any exact differential correction from the affine/chart comparison. Arbitrary ratio-dependent coefficients would generally destroy closedness. The raw trace has not been shown literally to equal $(0,0,1)$.

#### Formal checks and attached reproduction packet

`ContactSpanInverse.lean` uses only `Std` and kernel-checked `decide` to prove all 2,304 entries of the displayed 48-by-48 inverse identity; a separate `leanchecker` replay passed. Python links its literals to the audited jet minor. This does not formalize the recurrence, lifting or Hodge-theoretic interpretation. `CyclicSuspension.lean` proves the polynomial conversion identities conditional on a supplied twisted core primitive; it does not supply that primitive. Both files use only the standard axioms reported in the packet, with no `sorry`, added axiom or `native_decide`.

The accompanying ZIP contains `exact-core.md`, `trace-reduction.md`, both Lean sources, portable Python generators and independent checks, finite data, logs, and `REPRODUCE.md`. Running `python3 reproduce.py` performs the nine finite calculation stages. General proofs are referenced to the book rather than duplicated in the packet.

This is ChatGPT-assisted work for `benediamond`, including separate AI-agent arithmetic and mathematical audits. The [character calculation](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/discussions/120#discussioncomment-19150610) identifies the target sector. The [denominator investigations by `kejace`](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/discussions/120#discussioncomment-19345483) concern complementary restrictions; this construction has not extracted a denominator or rechecked those exclusions.
